title: CABIN ALTITUDE WARNING or Rapid Depressurization
ref: QRH NNC 2.1 (NG & MAX) · NNC 0.1 Emergency Descent · SOP 2.6

flash.title: Cruise FL370, night, over the Sahara.
flash.text: A dull bang, ears pop, a light mist fills the flight deck. The intermittent horn sounds, cabin altitude climbing fast.

steps.text: Don oxygen masks and set regulators to 100%.

steps.action: Hold in CLOSE until the outflow VALVE indication shows fully closed

steps.item: If cabin altitude is uncontrollable: Passenger signs
If cabin altitude is uncontrollable: PASS OXYGEN switch

steps.action: ►►Go to the Emergency Descent checklist on page 0.1

nums.s: Warning threshold · masks off at or below

trap: Diagnosing before the mask is on: mask and comms first, hypoxia gives no warning. And in flight, this intermittent horn is NOT the takeoff config warning.
then: Cabin uncontrollable → Emergency Descent (NNC 0.1) from memory
Cabin controllable → stay in MAN, masks may be removed at or below 10 000 ft cabin
Deferred items: Descent checklist, outflow VALVE in brief inputs
Pattern altitude: outflow VALVE OPEN until fully open to depressurize
SOP: CPT “… MEMORY ITEMS, I HAVE CONTROL”, F/O silences the horn, MAN + CLOSE
diff: Identical items NG/MAX. On NG, the CABIN ALTITUDE light is “if installed and operative”; on MAX it is always installed. The MAX QRH says “immediate action items” instead of “memory items”.

qcm.q: First memory item?
o: Don oxygen masks and set regulators to 100%.
Outflow VALVE switch … Hold in CLOSE
qcm.w: Masks at 100% first, then crew communication. Without oxygen, nothing else matters.

qcm.q: What do you do with the outflow VALVE switch?
o: Hold in CLOSE until the outflow VALVE indication shows fully closed
qcm.w: Hold in CLOSE until fully closed is indicated, after setting the mode selector to MAN.

qcm.q: When is PASS OXYGEN set to ON?
o: Always, as soon as the horn sounds
qcm.w: Conditional step 5: if cabin altitude is uncontrollable → Passenger signs ON, PASS OXYGEN ON, then Emergency Descent.

qcm.q: Intermittent horn in flight at FL350: what is it?
qcm.w: The takeoff config horn is armed only on the ground. In flight, it indicates cabin altitude above 10 000 ft (FCTM 8).

qcm.q: When may the masks be removed?
o: As soon as the cabin is controllable
qcm.w: Step 6: cabin controllable, and once cabin altitude is at or below 10 000 ft, “Oxygen masks may be removed”.

sources.quote: 1 Don oxygen masks and set regulators to 100%. 2 Establish crew communications. 3 Pressurization mode selector . . . MAN
4 Outflow VALVE switch . . . Hold in CLOSE until the outflow VALVE indication shows fully closed
If cabin altitude is uncontrollable: Passenger signs . . . ON PASS OXYGEN switch . . . ON ►►Go to the Emergency Descent checklist
When the cabin altitude is at or below 10,000 feet: Oxygen masks may be removed.
If this horn is activated in flight, it indicates that the cabin altitude has exceeded 10,000 feet.
Call “CABIN ALTITUDE WARNING or RAPID DEPRESSURIZATION MEMORY ITEMS, I HAVE CONTROL”

title: ENGINE FIRE or Engine Severe Damage or Separation

flash.title: Initial climb, runway 23 DAAG, 800 ft.
flash.text: Fire bell rings, red FIRE WARN lights on, engine 2 fire switch illuminated. Airplane under control, gear up.

steps.item: If the engine fire switch or ENG OVERHEAT light is illuminated: Engine fire switch (affected engine)
steps.action: Rotate to the stop and hold for 1 second

nums.s: Rotate to the stop and hold
Then rotate to the other stop if still illuminated

trap: Acting fast… on the wrong engine. Every “Confirm” item needs both pilots' agreement: PM's hand on the control, PF confirms, then action.
then: On the ground → Engine Fire on the Ground (Back Cover.2)
In flight, still illuminated after 30 s → rotate to the other stop, 1 s
Heavy vibration persists → reduce airspeed and descend without delay
ISOLATION VALVE CLOSE, affected-side PACK OFF, APU BLEED OFF, APU START
TA (MAX) / TA ONLY (NG), nearest suitable airport, One Engine Inoperative Landing
diff: Identical items. MAX: added condition “Engine failure with smoke or fumes in the flight deck or cabin” (LRD); CAB/UTIL + IFE/PASS SEAT load shed if no APU; note 50% N1 minimum if wing anti-ice above FL220. NNC 8.10 on NG, 8.2 on MAX.

qcm.q: Correct order of items 2 to 4?
o: Fire switch Pull → Thrust lever Close → Start lever CUTOFF
Thrust lever Close → Start lever CUTOFF → Fire switch Pull
Start lever CUTOFF → Thrust lever Close → Fire switch Pull
Thrust lever Close → Fire switch Pull → Start lever CUTOFF
qcm.w: A/T Disengage, Thrust lever Close, Start lever CUTOFF, Fire switch Pull, then Rotate if still illuminated.

qcm.q: When is the fire switch rotated in the memory items?
o: If the engine fire switch or ENG OVERHEAT light is illuminated
qcm.w: Conditional step 5: if the fire switch or ENG OVERHEAT light is illuminated → Rotate to the stop and hold for 1 second.

qcm.q: Fire switch still illuminated 30 s after the first rotation. Action?
o: Rotate to the other stop and hold for 1 second
Rotate to the same stop again
qcm.w: Step 7: rotate to the other stop to discharge the second bottle, hold 1 second.

qcm.q: Per SOP, minimum height for engine fire memory items after takeoff?
qcm.w: Airplane under control, gear up, safe altitude reached (minimum 400 ft AGL).

qcm.q: Engine fire on the ground. Which checklist after step 5?
o: Engine Fire on the Ground (Back Cover.2)
qcm.w: Step 6 “Choose one: On the ground” → Engine Fire on the Ground, on the QRH back cover.

sources.quote: 1 Autothrottle (if engaged) . . . Disengage 2 Thrust lever (affected engine) . . . Confirm . . . Close 3 Engine start lever (affected engine) . . . Confirm . . . CUTOFF
4 Engine fire switch (affected engine) . . . Confirm . . . Pull ... 5 If the engine fire switch or ENG OVERHEAT light is illuminated: ... Rotate to the stop and hold for 1 second
•Engine failure with smoke or fumes in the flight deck or cabin.
If after 30 seconds the engine fire switch or ENG OVERHEAT light stays illuminated: ... Rotate to the other stop and hold for 1 second
a safe altitude has been attained (minimum 400 feet AGL) accomplish the NNC memory items.
Note: If wing anti-ice is needed above FL220, maintain a minimum of 50% N1.

title: Engine Limit or Surge or Stall
ref: QRH NNC 7.2 (NG & MAX) · FCTM ch.8 Loss of Engine Thrust Control

flash.title: Climbing through FL180, heavy rain.
flash.text: Several dull bangs, light vibration. Engine 1 EGT rising toward redline, N1 fluctuating and no longer following the thrust lever.

steps.action: Confirm … Retard until engine indications stay within limits or the thrust lever is closed

trap: Retarding the thrust lever without confirming the engine, or shutting it down outright: retard only until back within limits. If the engine runs at reduced thrust: do not use FMC performance predictions, and set the transponder to TA.
then: Parameters stabilized and EGT stable/decreasing → advance slowly; do RPM/EGT follow?
Engine normal, or reduced thrust without surge → continue (TA / TA ONLY if reduced thrust)
Abnormal or EGT increasing → Engine start lever CUTOFF (Confirm), affected-side PACK OFF
APU START, balance fuel, ISOLATION VALVE Verify AUTO
Restart possible if N1 rotation and no abnormal vibration → Engine In-Flight Start
diff: Identical items. MAX: TA (NG: TA ONLY), CAB/UTIL + IFE/PASS SEAT load shed if APU unavailable, 50% N1 note above FL220. In-Flight Start at 7.24 (NG) / 7.26 (MAX).

qcm.q: Checklist item 2?
o: Thrust lever … Confirm … Retard until engine indications stay within limits or the thrust lever is closed
qcm.w: Retard until back within limits or until the thrust lever is closed; no immediate shutdown.

qcm.q: First item?
qcm.w: A/T is disengaged first so it doesn't drive the affected engine's thrust lever back up.

qcm.q: After the memory items, EGT keeps increasing. Next step?
o: Go to step 7: Engine start lever CUTOFF
qcm.w: Step 3: “Engine indications are abnormal or EGT continues to increase” → step 7, engine shutdown after confirmation.

qcm.q: Engine running at reduced thrust without surge. Per the QRH?
o: Transponder TA (MAX) / TA ONLY (NG) and no FMC predictions
Shut down the engine as a precaution
qcm.w: “Do not use FMC performance predictions” and transponder TA to avoid climb commands beyond capability.

qcm.q: Restart condition per the QRH?
o: If there is N1 rotation and no abnormal airframe vibration
qcm.w: “A restart may be attempted if there is N1 rotation and no abnormal airframe vibration.”

sources.quote: 1 Autothrottle (if engaged) . . . Disengage 2 Thrust lever (affected engine) . . . Confirm . . . Retard until engine indications stay within limits or the thrust lever is closed
Engine indications are abnormal or EGT continues to increase: ►►Go to step 7
Note: If wing anti-ice is needed above FL220, maintain a minimum of 50% N1.
A restart may be attempted if there is N1 rotation and no abnormal airframe vibration.
The Engine Limit or Surge or Stall NNC is written to include this malfunction.

title: Loss Of Thrust On Both Engines

flash.title: Descending through FL290, CB, very heavy rain.
flash.text: Both N1s collapse, amber ENG FAIL on both engines, displays flicker. Unusual silence on the flight deck.

steps.item: When EGT decreases: Engine start levers (both)
If EGT reaches a redline or there is no increase in EGT within 30 seconds: Engine start lever (affected engine)
If EGT again reaches a redline or there is no increase in EGT within 30 seconds,

trap: Starting the APU before the memory items: the FCTM calls for the memory items first to take advantage of high N2. No cross-confirmation procedure for this checklist (SOP).
then: Speed: 275 kt at/above FL270, 300 kt below
Slow acceleration possible: if N2 rises and EGT within limits, do not interrupt
APU START without waiting for relight, then APU GEN (both) ON one at a time
No relight: windmill if N2 ≥ 11% (NG) / 8.5% (MAX), otherwise starter assist with APU bleed
Engine stabilized: thrust lever Advance slowly, GEN ON
diff: Identical items. Reference items: windmill N2 threshold 11% (NG) vs 8.5% (MAX); MAX has you select an engine and set ENG HYD PUMP (selected engine) OFF before the restart, then ENG HYD PUMP ON and YAW DAMPER ON.

qcm.q: First memory item?
qcm.w: FLT first (ignition), then start levers CUTOFF, then IDLE when EGT decreases.

qcm.q: When are the start levers returned to IDLE detent?
qcm.w: Step 3: “When EGT decreases: Engine start levers (both) … IDLE detent”.

qcm.q: No EGT rise 30 s after IDLE. Action?
o: Engine start lever (affected engine) … Confirm … CUTOFF, then IDLE detent
Increase speed to 300 kt and wait
qcm.w: Step 4: CUTOFF then IDLE detent, repeat if EGT reaches redline or does not rise within 30 s.

qcm.q: Target speed at FL300?
qcm.w: At or above FL270: 275 kt. Below FL270: 300 kt.

qcm.q: N2 threshold to attempt a windmill start on the 737 MAX?
qcm.w: MAX: N2 ≥ 8.5% → windmill. NG: 11%. Below that, starter assist if APU bleed available.

sources.quote: 1 ENGINE START switches (both) . . . FLT 2 Engine start levers (both) . . . CUTOFF 3 When EGT decreases: Engine start levers (both) . . . IDLE detent
4 If EGT reaches a redline or there is no increase in EGT within 30 seconds: Engine start lever (affected engine) . . . Confirm . . . CUTOFF, then IDLE detent
At or above FL270, set airspeed to 275 knots. Below FL270, set airspeed to 300 knots.
N2 is at or above 11%: Attempt a windmill start.
N2 is at or above 8.5%: Attempt a windmill start.
Initiate the memory portion of the LOSS OF THRUST ON BOTH ENGINES NNC before attempting an APU start
This does not apply to the loss of Thrust on Both Engines checklist.

title: Aborted Engine Start
ref: QRH NNC 7.1 (NG & MAX) · FCOM NP.21 Engine Start

flash.title: On stand in Oran, starting engine 2.
flash.text: Start lever to IDLE. N2 hangs, EGT climbs very fast toward the start limit. The F/O keeps a hand on the start lever.

trap: Returning ENGINE START to GRD while N2 is still spinning down: wait for N2 < 20%. And never reopen the start lever to “save” a start.
then: ENGINE START switch still in GRD → motor 60 s, then OFF
Switch already OFF → wait for N2 < 20%, GRD, motor 60 s, OFF
Abort criteria (FCOM): N1/N2 not rising after EGT rise, no oil pressure at idle, no EGT rise within 15 s, EGT approaching start limit
3 consecutive aborted starts → 15 min cooling
diff: Identical item. On MAX (LEAP-1B), the EEC has automatic ground protection (hot start, stall, EGT exceedance, wet start) that cuts fuel and ignition; it does not operate in flight.

qcm.q: The only memory item?
qcm.w: Single memory item: start lever CUTOFF. Motoring is part of the reference items.

qcm.q: ENGINE START switch is OFF. Before returning it to GRD?
o: Wait for N2 to drop below 20%
qcm.w: Step 3: “After N2 decreases below 20%” → GRD, motor 60 s, then OFF.

qcm.q: Required motoring time?
qcm.w: “Motor the engine for 60 seconds.”

qcm.q: Which is NOT an FCOM abort criterion?
o: N2 at 25% when opening the start lever
No oil pressure once the engine is stabilized at idle
No EGT rise 15 s after IDLE detent
EGT rapidly approaching the start limit
qcm.w: 25% N2 is the normal condition for opening the start lever, not an abort criterion.

qcm.q: After 3 consecutive aborted starts?
qcm.w: FCOM limitations: “After three consecutive aborted start attempts, a 15-minute cooling period is required”.

sources.quote: 1 Engine start lever (affected engine) . . . CUTOFF
3 After N2 decreases below 20%: ENGINE START switch (affected engine) . . . GRD Motor the engine for 60 seconds.
the EGT does not increase by 15 seconds after the engine start lever is moved to IDLE detent
After three consecutive aborted start attempts, a 15-minute cooling period is required.
The EEC turns off the ignition and shuts off fuel to the engine for an impending hot start or stall.

title: ENGINE OVERHEAT

flash.title: Cruise FL350, daytime.
flash.text: MASTER CAUTION, OVHT/DET on the annunciator. ENG 1 OVERHEAT light on, no fire bell. Engine parameters normal.

steps.item: If the ENG OVERHEAT light stays illuminated:
steps.action: ►►Go to the ENGINE FIRE or Engine Severe Damage or Separation checklist

trap: Shutting the engine down by reflex: only close the thrust lever. If the light goes out, the engine keeps running at reduced thrust.
then: Light stays on → ENGINE FIRE or Engine Severe Damage or Separation
Light out → reduced thrust to keep it out, no FMC predictions
Transponder TA (MAX) / TA ONLY (NG)
MAX: avoid icing, engine anti-ice unavailable on the affected side
diff: Identical items. MAX adds: “Avoid icing conditions. Engine anti-ice is not available on the affected engine.” and do not run ENGINE COWL VALVE or TAI INDICATION. ENGINE FIRE reference page 8.10 (NG) / 8.2 (MAX).

qcm.q: ENGINE OVERHEAT item 2?
o: Thrust lever … Retard until within limits
qcm.w: A/T Disengage, then thrust lever closed. No fuel cutoff in the memory items.

qcm.q: ENG OVERHEAT light stays on after closing the thrust lever?
o: Go to ENGINE FIRE or Engine Severe Damage or Separation
Engine Limit or Surge or Stall
qcm.w: Step 3: light still on → ENGINE FIRE checklist, fire switch included.

qcm.q: The light goes out. What about the engine?
o: Run the engine at reduced thrust to keep the light extinguished
qcm.w: Keep the engine at reduced thrust so the light stays out.

qcm.q: MAX-specific reference item?
o: Avoid icing: engine anti-ice unavailable on the affected side
qcm.w: QRH MAX 8.7 step 6: “Avoid icing conditions. Engine anti-ice is not available on the affected engine.”

qcm.q: First item?
qcm.w: As for ENGINE FIRE and Engine Limit: start by disengaging the A/T.

sources.quote: 1 Autothrottle (if engaged) . . . Disengage 2 Thrust lever (affected engine) . . . Confirm . . . Close 3 If the ENG OVERHEAT light stays illuminated: ►►Go to the ENGINE FIRE or Engine Severe Damage or Separation checklist on page 8.10
4 If the ENG OVERHEAT light extinguishes: Run the engine at reduced thrust to keep the light extinguished.
Avoid icing conditions. Engine anti-ice is not available on the affected engine.

title: APU FIRE
ref: QRH NNC 8.1 (NG & MAX) · FCTM ch.8 Evacuation

flash.title: Turnaround in Algiers, APU running.
flash.text: Fire bell rings, FIRE WARN lights on, APU fire switch illuminated. Engines shut down, passengers boarding.

steps.action: Confirm … Pull, rotate to the stop, and hold for 1 second

nums.s: Rotate to the stop and hold

trap: Doing only “Pull” as for an engine: for the APU, the single item chains Pull, rotate to the stop and hold 1 s. Then APU switch OFF.
then: APU fire switch extinguishes → checklist complete
Switch stays illuminated → plan to land at the nearest suitable airport
On the ground, if evacuating: Evacuation checklist (Back Cover.4)

qcm.q: First APU FIRE item?
o: APU fire switch … Confirm … Pull, rotate to the stop, and hold for 1 second
qcm.w: Pull, rotate and hold 1 s in a single item, before switching the APU OFF.

qcm.q: Second item?
qcm.w: Item 2: APU switch OFF. The dashed line follows.

qcm.q: APU fire switch stays illuminated in flight?
o: Plan to land at the nearest suitable airport
qcm.w: Step 4: “Plan to land at the nearest suitable airport.”

qcm.q: How long to hold the switch rotated?
qcm.w: “Rotate to the stop, and hold for 1 second.”

qcm.q: APU fire switch extinguishes after discharge. Next?
o: Plan to land at the nearest suitable airport
qcm.w: Step 3 “APU fire switch extinguishes” → ■■■■ end of checklist.

sources.quote: 1 APU fire switch . . . Confirm . . . Pull, rotate to the stop, and hold for 1 second 2 APU switch . . . OFF
APU fire switch stays illuminated: ►►Go to step 4 4 Plan to land at the nearest suitable airport.
If an APU fire indication exists or a fire is reported in or near the APU, discharge the APU fire bottle.
